record.context_brief: Maximality of sup norm on C[0,1]
record.original_question: Consider the Banach space C[0,1] of continuous real-valued functions on the interval [0,1] with the supremum norm. Is this supremum norm maximal, meaning that whenever an equivalent F-norm has a larger group of rotations, the two groups of rotations must in fact coincide?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM U. - Is the norm sup in the space C[0, 1] of continuous real on interval [0, 1] maximal ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C[0,1]$ denote the Banach space of all continuous real-valued functions on the interval $[0,1]$ equipped with the supremum norm $\|f\|_\infty=\sup_{t\in[0,1]}|f(t)|$. Recall that an $F$-norm on a real vector space $X$ is a functional $\|\cdot\|:X\to[0,\infty)$ such that $\|x\|=0$ iff $x=0$, $\|\alpha x\|=\|x\|$ for every scalar $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|=1$, $\|x+y\|\le\|x\|+\|y\|$, and $\|\alpha_n x\|\to 0$ whenever $\alpha_n\to 0$ in scalars. Two $F$-norms on $X$ are equivalent if they induce the same topology. The group of rotations of an $F$-normed space $(X,\|\cdot\|)$ is the group of all surjective linear isometries of $(X,\|\cdot\|)$. An $F$-norm $\|\cdot\|$ on $X$ is called maximal if, whenever $\|\cdot\|'$ is an equivalent $F$-norm on $X$ whose group of rotations contains the group of rotations of $\|\cdot\|$, then the two groups of rotations coincide.

Question: Is the supremum norm on $C[0,1]$ maximal in this sense?
artifact.status_search_result: Maximality of the sup norm on $C(K)$ spaces has been investigated by Wood, Pelczynski–Rolewicz, Cabello Sánchez, and others; Cabello Sánchez (BLMS, 2005) showed that the complex $C_0(\Omega)$ is convex-transitive when $\Omega$ is a connected manifold without boundary, and various related convex-transitivity/maximality results are known for $\ell_\infty/c_0$, $L_\infty$, and $C(\Delta)$. However, no search result located definitively settles the maximality of the sup norm on the real space $C[0,1]$ (whose underlying compact space has boundary). The status of this specific question could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: Convex transitive norms on spaces of continuous functions (Cabello Sánchez)
status_evidence.snippet: The main result is that the complex C_0(Ω) is convex-transitive in its natural supremum norm if Ω is a connected manifold without boundary.
status_evidence.claim: Related convex-transitivity/maximality results are known for various C(K) spaces, but [0,1] (which has boundary) is not directly covered.

status_evidence.title: On an isomorphic Banach–Mazur rotation problem and maximal norms in Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Maximal norms in Banach spaces; a norm is maximal if no equivalent norm has a strictly larger isometry group.
status_evidence.claim: The notion of maximal norm is an active topic; status for sup norm on C[0,1] not explicitly resolved here.
